sources.author: pearce et al.
sources.finding: copilot outputs can contain exploitable patterns, and detection depends on task and analysis coverage.
sources.comparison: Our matched three-language corpus and explicit positive/negative controls extend the assessment context. Different models, prompts and examined weaknesses prevent direct rate comparisons.

sources.author: khoury et al.
sources.finding: security-sensitive tasks and subsequent prompting expose different security concerns in chatgpt outputs.
sources.comparison: our fixed first-response design separates initial outputs from repair dialogue. differences in model, tasks and security instructions prevent direct rate comparisons.

sources.author: schreiber and tippe
sources.status: full author manuscript inspected; publisher citation year 2026
sources.finding: codeql identifies weaknesses in ai-attributed repository files; repository attribution and surrounding context constrain interpretation.
sources.comparison: our directly logged matched functions reduce uncertainty about collection provenance and add java. they do not reproduce repository integration or attribution conditions.

sources.author: tihanyi et al.
sources.finding: A C-language benchmark assesses generated programs through formal verification with ESBMC in an unbounded setting, subject to execution limits.
sources.comparison: The generated C programs, examined properties and formal-verification instrument differ from our matched functions and frozen static rule pack. The study informs our distinction between executable screening and adequate semantic coverage; its rates are not a language-effect baseline for our corpus.

sources.author: aydın and bahtiyar
sources.status: Full 14-page preprint inspected, including methods, results and limitations.
sources.finding: A matched multi-model, multi-language prompt design uses Semgrep, Snyk and SonarCloud, followed by manual review; CWE distributions and model rankings depend on language and the metric used.
sources.comparison: Our study extends the measurement discussion with explicit positive and negative controls. Our smaller functions, security-relevant task constraints, single visible generator and one frozen scanner configuration differ from their broader functional prompts and multi-tool analysis. The observed rates cannot establish a direct replication or contradiction.

sources.author: fu et al.
sources.finding: repository-derived python and javascript snippets contain weaknesses assessed with language-specific tools and manual warning filtering.
sources.comparison: Our separate reporting of scanner alerts and source-level mechanisms supports the distinction between candidate warnings and assessed weaknesses. Matched task descriptions and Java extend the comparison context without establishing a prevalence difference from repository snippets.

sources.author: basic and giaretta
sources.status: full review manuscript inspected; version 4; journal publication not verified
sources.finding: the review identifies heterogeneous generation, detection and remediation evaluations.
sources.comparison: the gap between scanner silence and missed known positives illustrates why tool coverage and outcome definitions must accompany a security result.
